verdict.rationale: Graphite documents custom rules that tell Graphite Agent what guidelines to follow when reviewing code, and its AI reviews automatically run on every new PR in selected repositories. That is a first-party, agent-driven per-PR review that can be steered by user-defined rules. However, nothing in the evidence shows these rules act as discrete pre-merge checks with pass/fail status that gate merging, or that they are written in free-form plain language like 'docs updated' or 'tests cover new paths'. missing for 10: documented pass/fail pre-merge check status or merge gating from custom rules, explicit plain-language rule authoring examples, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I define custom agentic pre-merge checks in plain language — 'docs updated', 'tests cover new paths' — that run on every PR

citations.quote: Custom rules allow you to define explicit guidelines for Graphite Agent to follow when reviewing your code.
Graphite Agent will now automatically review all new pull requests in the selected repositories
AI reviews analyze every pull request in your repositories, identifying potential issues and suggesting fixes instantly
